title: Give validate a way to read the App's window state without UI Automation
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C1 (derived): the App has a flag that writes the scan ending and totals to a file or stdout: missing
C2 (derived, alternative to C1): an App test project exists that can read MainWindow state without UI Automation: missing
C3 (derived): validate can read the published exe's own window state, which was never read during SL-020: missing
Repo's own tests and build, as a measure of state: unknown

The recorded storage line says 'nothing is saved to disk'. This design writes a small JSON diagnostic file, but only when `--report <file>` is passed, and it holds totals and the root, never a listing. I built the file form on the reading that the line covers scan data and not an opt-in diagnostic. If the person reads it as covering any disk write, the report must move to stdout, which changes the launch contract, and the exit-3 and delete-first machinery drops out.

File output versus stdout output. Both were measured to work (`& exe | Out-String` waits and captures; Start-Process redirection also works), and only the file form was spiked on the real exe. The file is chosen for that reason, but stdout would leave nothing on disk and remove the stale-file, atomic-write and exit-3 machinery.
Where the once-only ending guard lives: in MainWindow (the proposal) or in the App's report handler (chosen). This is boundary placement.
A committed reader script (composer-added) versus the recipe living only as a header comment in WindowReport.cs and being re-derived by each validate run.
Keeping the `core` section beside `window`. It helps diagnose which side is wrong, but it invites a lazy checker to verify Core instead of the window. It is kept and labelled as not an oracle.
WindowReport as its own class versus inlining the reading in App.xaml.cs. The separate file lets architecture rule 1 name one file, but it is a layering choice.
